Hi Karthik,

Really sorry — our lead engineer had an emergency this morning and we need to pull the team from next Tuesday's hands-on POC kickoff. We have no bandwidth for a live session that day anymore.

I still want to run this POC — the goal is to validate routing/latency under our expected traffic and exercise the prompt reviews you recommended — but we need to either push the live session or go async first.

Could you propose a couple of alternative windows (late-week or next-week mornings PST)? If you can share an async runbook we can follow to get the initial routing and prompt review started, that would help keep momentum.

Thanks,

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the emergency. Totally understand.

Two quick things we can do to keep momentum:

1) Propose two live windows (we’ll keep them focused — 90-minute hands-on):
   - Thu 2027-09-16 09:00–10:30 PT (preferred: routing + load test primer)
   - Mon 2027-09-20 08:00–09:30 PT (fallback)

2) Async runbook: I attached a concise staged runbook and a one-page agenda that walks your team through the prompt review, routing verification, and a mini load test you can run on your schedule. If you want, we can run the load test from our side too — Marissa can coordinate the traffic shaping.

If neither window works, tell me two times that do and we’ll move. If you want to split the work, we can do an async primer now and follow with a short live session just for the final verification.

Quick ask: does your team have a preferred concurrency target for the mini load test (e.g., 50 rps, 200 rps)? That'll determine how we stage caching and batching settings.

Cheers,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.ai

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Sara's note. If they pick 9/16 we should plan to:

- Prep a short prompt review session (30 min) focused on reranking/routing knobs.
- Run a 10-min smoke load at 20 rps from Redwood to validate KV cache behavior.
- Keep a fallback plan to run the full load test asynchronously if time runs out.

Ben — can you prepare the traffic script and a one-click run command we can trigger if they want Redwood to drive the load? Keep it conservative unless they give a target.

I'll loop legal if they ask for any test-data controls, but given this is a short primer standard sandbox data should be fine.

-Marissa

I'll package the run command and a small README and attach to the calendar invite. If Acme wants us to run the smoke test, we can do it in the first 15 minutes of the meeting so we still have time for prompt tuning.

-Ben
